cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus asks them to believe in Him as well. He says, “You believe in God; believe in Me as well.” (John 14:1) Notice He doesn't ask them to trade one for the other. He says “as well,” so it's both, side by side.

The answer is place. Jesus says, “…I am going there to prepare a place for you?” (John 14:2) He's talking about a spot made ready for the disciples, in His Father's house. One little word, friends, and it holds a lot of comfort.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.” (John 14:3) He goes ahead, and then He comes back. The point is that they end up where He is.

The answer is that Thomas says they don't even know where Jesus is going. He says, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?” (John 14:5) He says out loud what I bet a few others were thinking. I think a lot of us would have kept nodding.

The answer is the way and the truth and the life. Jesus answers Thomas, “I am the way and the truth and the life.” (John 14:6) Thomas asked about a way, and Jesus points to Himself. It's not directions to a place, friends, it's a Person.

The answer is False. Right after saying He is the way and the truth and the life, Jesus says, “No one comes to the Father except through Me.” (John 14:6) He doesn't offer Thomas a menu of ways. He gives one, and it's Himself.
The answer is enough for us. Philip says, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” (John 14:8) He asks for one thing and says it would be enough. Jesus has more to say about that.

The answer is that Jesus asks, “How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?” (John 14:9) Just before that, He says that anyone who has seen Him has seen the Father. So He answers Philip's request with a question about Philip's own words.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works.” (John 14:10) The Father is at work in Him. Whatever He says, it isn't a solo act.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…or at least believe on account of the works themselves.” (John 14:11) He gives them another reason to believe. If His word isn't enough yet, the works are right there to look at.

The answer is name. Jesus says, “And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.” (John 14:13) The asking is in His name. And the purpose He gives is that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

The answer is another Advocate. Jesus says the Father will give them “another Advocate” to be with them forever (John 14:16). A few verses later He names Him as the Holy Spirit (John 14:26). So they won't be on their own, friends.
The answer is False. Jesus says of the Spirit, “But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.” (John 14:17) The world neither sees Him nor knows Him. The disciples know Him.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me.” (John 14:19) The world and the disciples get different news there. Listen for that “but,” bakers.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.” (John 14:21) The Father loves that person, and Jesus loves him too. That's quite a table to be sitting at.

The answer is that Judas asks why Jesus will reveal Himself to them and not to the world. Judas (not Iscariot) says, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?” (John 14:22) Jesus has just said He will reveal Himself to the one who loves Him. Then Jesus replies to Judas in the very next verse. That's a question worth asking.

The answers are word and home. Jesus says, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word.” (John 14:23) That's the first blank. A person who loves Him keeps what He says. Jesus says the Father and He “…will come to him and make Our home with him.” (John 14:23) That's the second blank, friends. The Father and Jesus making a home with the one who loves Him, and I think that's the best part of the verse.

The answer is that the teaching comes from the One who sent Him. Jesus says, “The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.” (John 14:24) The Father is the source of what the disciples are hearing.

The answer is True. Jesus says the Advocate “…will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.” (John 14:26) Teaching and reminding, both coming from the Holy Spirit. I walk into the pantry and forget why every single time, so a promise like that sounds wonderful to me.

The answer is that He does not give as the world gives. Jesus says, “I do not give to you as the world gives.” (John 14:27) He says it right after “Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you.” His peace is His own, friends.

The answer is rejoice. Jesus says, “If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father…” (John 14:28) That's the word that fills the blank. He gives the reason too: “…because the Father is greater than I.”

The answer is so the world may know He loves the Father. Jesus says, “But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father.” (John 14:31) He gives the reason Himself. Obeying the Father shows His love for the Father.
